reporter.vector: promoterless luciferase (pGL4.10-style) or GFP for FACS-based screening; luciferase for arrayed compound screens, GFP for pooled CRISPRa
controls: Promoterless vector: establishes the floor. Without it you cannot tell activation from vector background.
Constitutive promoter (CMV/EF1a): establishes the ceiling and reports transfection or transduction efficiency per well.

Scrambled-motif variant of your top predicted element: the single most informative control here. If a drug induces the wild-type reporter but not the mutant, the effect runs through that element. If it induces both, the mechanism is elsewhere and the prediction was wrong.
Dual-reporter normalisation (Renilla or similar) to separate real induction from changes in cell number or general translation — cytotoxic compounds otherwise read as repressors.
reporter.caveat: An episomal reporter lacks the chromatin context of the endogenous locus. A hit should be confirmed at the native gene by RT-qPCR before it is believed.

compounds.design: Arrayed, 384-well, 8-point dose-response on the actives. Single-concentration primary screens at 10 uM produce a cytotoxicity-dominated hit list; dose-response separates real induction from cells dying.
compounds.counter_screen: Run the same plate against a constitutive-promoter reporter. Anything that moves both is affecting transcription or translation globally, not your promoter, and that is the majority of primary hits.
compounds.note: A full-library screen is unbiased and will find mechanisms this package cannot predict — that is its advantage, not a criticism of it. Use the cherry-pick list to get an answer in a week; run the full library when you want the answer you did not expect.

expectations.compound_screen_hit_rate: 0.5-2% at a sensible threshold. Most primary hits are cytotoxic or assay-interfering; expect to lose 60-80% at counter-screen.
expectations.crispra_hit_rate: typically a handful of TFs from ~1,600. A screen returning hundreds of hits is reporting a global effect on the reporter, not specific regulation.
expectations.replicates: 3 biological replicates minimum; 2 gives you no estimate of variance and a Z' you cannot trust
expectations.quality_metric: Z' >= 0.5 between positive and negative controls before you screen anything. Below that the screen cannot distinguish a real hit from noise and running it wastes the library.
expectations.what_a_negative_result_means: If no TF in a genome-wide CRISPRa screen activates your reporter, the promoter fragment is probably not sufficient — the regulation likely lives in an enhancer outside your window. Widen it (--upstream 50000) or use the endogenous locus.

reporter.insert: 3:46367670-46373669 (5000 bp upstream / 1000 bp downstream of the ENST00000445772 TSS)
reporter.vector: promoterless luciferase (pGL4.10-style) or GFP for FACS-based screening; luciferase for arrayed compound screens, GFP for pooled CRISPRa
controls: Promoterless vector: establishes the floor. Without it you cannot tell activation from vector background.
Constitutive promoter (CMV/EF1a): establishes the ceiling and reports transfection or transduction efficiency per well.

Scrambled-motif variant of your top predicted element: the single most informative control here. If a drug induces the wild-type reporter but not the mutant, the effect runs through that element. If it induces both, the mechanism is elsewhere and the prediction was wrong.
Dual-reporter normalisation (Renilla or similar) to separate real induction from changes in cell number or general translation — cytotoxic compounds otherwise read as repressors.
reporter.caveat: An episomal reporter lacks the chromatin context of the endogenous locus. A hit should be confirmed at the native gene by RT-qPCR before it is believed.

crispra.approach: dCas9-VP64 with SAM (MS2-p65-HSF1) or dCas9-VPR for stronger activation

library.focused: 20 TFs prioritised by this run (RARA, ESRRG, ESRRB, RORB, NFIA, NR1I3, RORC, CTCF, RORA, PRDM5...)
library.genome_wide: ~1,600 human TFs (Calabrese or a TF-focused sublibrary). Run this if the focused set comes back empty — an unbiased screen is the only thing that finds a factor nobody has associated with your promoter.
library.coverage: 3-5 sgRNAs per gene, >=500 cells per guide at transduction, MOI ~0.3 to keep single integrations

crispra.note: Guides listed target YOUR promoter directly, for a positive-control arm proving the reporter can be activated at all. The library guides target the TFs. Run these through CRISPOR or CHOPCHOP for off-target scoring before ordering — no off-target analysis is done here.
crispra.readout: FACS sort GFP-high vs GFP-low, then sequence guide abundance; or arrayed luciferase for a focused set

libraries: Prestwick Chemical Library (~1,520 approved drugs, high chemical and pharmacological diversity)
NCATS Pharmaceutical Collection (NPC) — free, and the most complete approved set
compounds.design: Arrayed, 384-well, 8-point dose-response on the actives. Single-concentration primary screens at 10 uM produce a cytotoxicity-dominated hit list; dose-response separates real induction from cells dying.
compounds.counter_screen: Run the same plate against a constitutive-promoter reporter. Anything that moves both is affecting transcription or translation globally, not your promoter, and that is the majority of primary hits.
compounds.note: A full-library screen is unbiased and will find mechanisms this package cannot predict — that is its advantage, not a criticism of it. Use the cherry-pick list to get an answer in a week; run the full library when you want the answer you did not expect.

expectations.compound_screen_hit_rate: 0.5-2% at a sensible threshold. Most primary hits are cytotoxic or assay-interfering; expect to lose 60-80% at counter-screen.
expectations.crispra_hit_rate: typically a handful of TFs from ~1,600. A screen returning hundreds of hits is reporting a global effect on the reporter, not specific regulation.
expectations.replicates: 3 biological replicates minimum; 2 gives you no estimate of variance and a Z' you cannot trust
expectations.quality_metric: Z' >= 0.5 between positive and negative controls before you screen anything. Below that the screen cannot distinguish a real hit from noise and running it wastes the library.
expectations.what_a_negative_result_means: If no TF in a genome-wide CRISPRa screen activates your reporter, the promoter fragment is probably not sufficient — the regulation likely lives in an enhancer outside your window. Widen it (--upstream 50000) or use the endogenous locus.

lincs.summary: No LINCS signature found moving CCR5. Check whether CCR5 is expressed in the L1000 cell panel at all — if it is not, this says nothing about your drug.

notes: These are phenotypes associated with germline variation in this gene. They anticipate what raising or lowering it may do — including on-target adverse effects — but variants act lifelong while a drug does not, so developmental compensation confounds the comparison in a direction that cannot be predicted.

genetics.summary: Human genetic variation in CCR5 associates with: HIV-1 infection, COVID-19, type 1 diabetes mellitus. Read this as a preview of what modulating the gene may do, including the adverse effects — this is the reasoning that anticipated PCSK9 inhibition years before the trials.

notes: To test this link genetically: look for trans-eQTLs of RARA affecting CCR5 in eQTLGen (blood, n>30,000) or GTEx. A hit is strong causal evidence for the regulatory relationship. Absence is weak evidence against it — trans-eQTL detection needs very large samples and most real regulatory links are undetectable at current power.
